conclusion: Candidates 1 and 2 both fail. Candidate 1's objective is constant on its feasible set (t.x = u_0), so it optimises nothing and merely reads back a coordinate of its own input. Candidate 2 leaves the radical intact for every braid word tried, on both sides, because V spans a two-sided ideal; with <t,v> = tr_M(V) = 0 holding for any Gram, y_0 = 0 remains forced. A surviving formulation must change the COST vector, not the Gram.
